traveler: Theodor Reuss (Albert Karl Theodor Reuss, in religion Merlin Peregrinus, on the stage Charles Theodore)
title: The Paper Empire: Augsburg to Munich by way of every charter in Europe
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Augsburg, the innkeeper's son
stops.date_confidence: disputed: en.wikipedia gives 28 June 1855, de.wikipedia gives 28 July 1855. Both agree on the year and on Augsburg. The June date is carried here without preference between them.
stops.campa: In Augsburg the innkeeper Franz Xaver Reuss and his wife Eva Barbara Margaret Wagner have a son and name him Albert Karl Theodor. The English record puts the birth on the twenty-eighth of June; the German record puts it on the twenty-eighth of July. Neither gives ground. The boy grows up in a Bavarian public house, in the traffic of travellers and their talk, and will spend his adult life issuing documents that fix dates and titles with notarial exactness while his own first date stays double.
suggested_refs: Augsburg parish registers for 1855, not consulted for this journey

stops.name: Augsburg, the Kreis-Gewerbeschule and the druggist's counter
stops.date_confidence: inferred: de.wikipedia places the commercial school and the druggist's apprenticeship in his youth without giving a year. The 1870 date is a placeholder for the decade, not a documented enrolment.
stops.campa: He attends the commercial section of the Kreis-Gewerbeschule and is apprenticed to a druggist, learning weights, powders, and the Latin of the dispensary. The trade does not hold him. He has a voice, and a voice in Bavaria in the 1870s is a career, so he leaves the counter for the stage and takes the name Charles Theodore. The exact building is not identified in the sources consulted, and Augsburg's centre stands in for it. The apprenticeship leaves him a habit he keeps for life: measured quantities out of separate jars, combined into a single preparation.
suggested_refs: Records of the Augsburg Kreis-Gewerbeschule, commercial section, 1860s to 1870s

stops.name: Munich, presented to King Ludwig II
stops.date_confidence: legendary: en.wikipedia dates the introduction to 1873 and carries no citation for it; Peter-R. Koenig's archive puts the Bavarian court connection at 1883; de.wikipedia states that the acquaintances with Ludwig II and with Wagner cannot be historically substantiated. The pin marks Munich, not a documented meeting.
stops.campa: The story is that the young singer is brought before Ludwig II of Bavaria and enters, briefly, the orbit of the king who is building castles out of opera. Reuss will lean on it for fifty years. The German record answers that the acquaintance with Ludwig, like the acquaintance with Wagner, cannot be historically substantiated, and the English article that repeats the date carries no citation for it. The legend is part of the man all the same. He is a person to whom things are attributed, most often by himself.
suggested_refs: Court records of the household of Ludwig II, 1873 and 1883, not consulted

stops.name: Vienna, the singer's training and the lost voice
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Koenig's archive gives an operatic circuit of Vienna, Paris, Amsterdam and Quedlinburg across the 1870s and 1880s with no dates and no venues. The 1874 pin is a placeholder within that span.
stops.campa: He studies singing in Vienna and works the continental circuit as an operatic and variety performer. Koenig's archive lists the itinerary without venues: Vienna, Paris, Amsterdam, Quedlinburg. No playbill from any of these towns has been produced. Then illness takes the voice, the one asset demonstrably his own, and the career built on it closes. Everything he does afterwards he does with paper instead: charters, patents, constitutions, journals, letters of authority, every one of them signed and most of them dated to the day.
suggested_refs: Vienna theatre almanacs of the 1870s, searched for the stage name Charles Theodore

segments.name: London, Munich, and the First Orders

stops.name: Dublin, the bride's city
stops.date_confidence: attested year, unlocated: en.wikipedia gives the marriage and the later annulment for bigamy. Neither the day nor the place of the wedding is recorded in any source consulted, and the pin marks the bride's origin only.
stops.campa: Delphina Garbois comes from Dublin. Whether she is married in Dublin or in London the sources do not say, and the annulment for bigamy raises the question of whose earlier marriage was concealed without answering it. The pin marks her origin and nothing else. It is the first documented gap in a life that will accumulate them: an event that certainly happened, in one of two cities, on a day nobody recorded, between two people one of whom has left no other trace in the reachable record at all.
suggested_refs: General Register Office marriage indexes for England and for Ireland, 1876, not searched for this journey

stops.name: London, Freemasons' Hall: initiated in Pilger Lodge No. 238
stops.date_confidence: attested: de.wikipedia gives 9 November 1876; en.wikipedia gives the year only. The lodge and the constitution under the United Grand Lodge of England are agreed by both.
stops.campa: On the ninth of November the former singer is made a Freemason in Pilger Lodge No. 238, a German-speaking lodge working under the United Grand Lodge of England. It is the first of the affiliations and the only one whose body outlives him unchanged. Earlier in the year he has married Delphina Garbois, a marriage later annulled on the ground of bigamy. The meeting place is inferred from Freemasons' Hall in Great Queen Street; the sources name the lodge and the year, not the room.
sources: Grand Lodge of British Columbia and Yukon, biographical note on Reuss
suggested_refs: Membership registers of Pilger Lodge No. 238, Library and Museum of Freemasonry, London

stops.name: Munich, the war correspondent's claim
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Munich move (1878, en.wikipedia). The Balkan correspondence is dated 1878 to 1882 by de.wikipedia, which names no city and no dispatch and carries the claim among Reuss's self-reported credentials.
stops.campa: He moves to Munich. From here he says he writes for The Times as a war correspondent out of the Balkans, and later out of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The German record carries the claim among his own credentials and names no city, no dispatch, and no dateline; no byline in The Times has been produced. The pin is Munich, where he can be placed, rather than Sarajevo, where he cannot. He is twenty-three and has begun the practice of describing himself in print, in the third person, as a man of standing.
suggested_refs: The Times digital archive, 1878 to 1882, Balkan despatches, not searched for this journey

stops.name: Munich, the Bavarian Illuminati raised again
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1880 by both en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia, neither giving a month. The 1881 expulsion from Freemasonry for left-wing activity appears in de.wikipedia only and is not corroborated in English-language sourcing.
stops.campa: A century after Adam Weishaupt's order is suppressed by the Elector of Bavaria, Reuss joins an attempt to raise it again in the city where it was born. The attempt fails. It establishes the method he will use for the rest of his life: find a dead order with a famous name, obtain or manufacture a descent from it, and open subscriptions. In the following year the German record has him expelled from Freemasonry for left-wing political activity, an expulsion the English sourcing does not mention at all.
suggested_refs: Papers of the 1880 Munich Illuminati revival circle

stops.name: Bayreuth Festspielhaus, the Parsifal claim
stops.date_confidence: attested for the premiere, 26 July 1882 under Hermann Levi. Reuss's participation is described by de.wikipedia as merely alleged, and the sentence asserting it in en.wikipedia carries no citation.
stops.campa: Wagner's Parsifal has its premiere on the Green Hill under Hermann Levi, and Reuss says he sings in it. He will build a doctrine on the opera: that the Grail is not a cup but a body, that Wagner encoded a sexual mystery in the last work of his life, and that the Ordo Templi Orientis holds the key to it. The German record calls his participation merely alleged and the Wagner connection unsubstantiated. Thirty-two years later he publishes the reading anyway, in a pamphlet that becomes the order's central text.
stops.quote: Parsifal does not ask in the first act: What is the Graal, Parsifal asks, Who is the Graal?
stops.quote_source: Theodor Reuss, Parsifal and the Secret of the Graal Unveiled (1914), Main Part: The Unveiling of the Secret, written thirty-two years after this premiere; text as reproduced on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: Bayreuth Festival personnel lists for the 1882 Parsifal production

segments.name: The Socialist League and the Informer

stops.name: London, the Theosophical London Lodge
stops.date_confidence: membership attested for 1885 by de.wikipedia, which gives no month. The meeting with Blavatsky is undated in the source and cannot have taken place in London that year: she left India in March 1885, was in Naples by April, then Wurzburg, then Ostend, and reached London only in May 1887.
stops.campa: He joins the London Lodge of the Theosophical Society and is later said to have met Helena Blavatsky in it. Blavatsky is not in London in 1885. She leaves India in March, is in Naples by April, then Wurzburg, then Ostend, and does not arrive in London until May 1887. The lodge exists without her; the encounter, if it happens, happens later. Reuss and Blavatsky are two travellers of this atlas passing through the same rooms at Lansdowne Road and Avenue Road within two years of one another.
suggested_refs: Membership rolls of the London Lodge of the Theosophical Society, 1885 to 1888

stops.name: London, Great Queen Street: the Socialist League
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1885 by en.wikipedia, which gives no month; the June date is a placeholder. The address is the League's documented headquarters for 1885 and 1886, correcting a Farringdon Road pin in the research pool that belongs to the conferences of 1887 and later.
stops.campa: He sits on the executive of William Morris's Socialist League and works as its librarian and labour secretary. The League's headquarters in these years is at 24 Great Queen Street, a few hundred yards from the Masonic hall where he was initiated nine years earlier. He is at one and the same moment a Freemason, a Theosophist and a revolutionary socialist, drawing what income he can from each. The Prussian secret police, according to the accusation that ends this phase, are paying him as well.
suggested_refs: Socialist League archive, International Institute of Social History, Amsterdam

stops.name: London, expelled as a police spy
stops.date_confidence: disputed: en.wikipedia dates the expulsion 7 May 1886, de.wikipedia 10 May 1886. Neither sentence carries a citation in the article wikitext, and no primary expulsion notice was reachable. The 7 May date is carried without preference.
stops.campa: The League expels him as a police spy in the pay of the Prussian secret police. The German text of the resolution puts him out for dishonourable conduct and calls him an international police blackguard. The charge comes in the middle of the Peukert and Dave feud, where accusations of this kind are made freely and often without substance, and Peukert's Gruppe Autonomie publishes a rebuttal in the Anarchist. Nine months later Reuss uses Peukert himself to track down the arms smuggler Johann Neve.
suggested_refs: Minutes of the Socialist League council, May 1886; the Anarchist, 1886 rebuttal by the Gruppe Autonomie

stops.name: Belgium, the betrayal of Johann Neve
stops.date_confidence: attested for February 1887 by en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia; no day is given. The location within Belgium is not recorded in any source consulted, and the Brussels coordinate is a country-level placeholder rather than a documented site.
stops.campa: Through Peukert he reaches the arms smuggler Johann Neve and hands him to the German authorities. Neve is seized in Belgium and dies in German custody. This is the act that turns the accusation of the previous May from factional slander into something the record supports. No source consulted names the town, the street or the day; the pin sits at Brussels because Belgium is as close as the sources come. From here on Reuss is a man with a police connection and an occult career, and the two are never fully separated again.
suggested_refs: Belgian and Prussian police files on the arrest of Johann Neve, February 1887

stops.name: Berlin, Leopold Engel and the second Illuminati
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Engel collaboration from 1888 (en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia), with no month given, and for the pamphlet in 1887 (de.wikipedia, no month). The separation from Engel is dated 1902.
stops.campa: His first pamphlet, The Matrimonial Question, appears in 1887, and more than thirty works on freemasonry, occultism and esotericism will follow it. In Berlin he joins Leopold Engel in a second attempt at the Illuminati, this one lasting long enough to produce rituals, a periodical and, by 1902, a formal separation between the two men. The partnership teaches him what the Munich attempt did not. An order needs a printing arrangement more urgently than it needs members.
suggested_refs: Theodor Reuss, Die Ehefrage (1887); the Engel-Reuss Illuminatenorden papers

stops.name: Vienna, the conversations with Carl Kellner
stops.date_confidence: traditional: en.wikipedia dates the first discussions to 1895 without a month. Vienna is Kellner's city and is where the meeting is conventionally placed; no source documents a Reuss journey there for the purpose.
stops.campa: In Vienna the industrial chemist Carl Kellner, rich from a paper-pulp patent and interested in yoga, tantra and the Hermetic sciences, begins talking with Reuss about a new body: an academy of masonry that would gather the high degrees of the fringe rites into one house and teach, at its summit, a sexual secret. Kellner supplies the doctrine and the money. Reuss supplies the paperwork and the appetite for titles. Out of these conversations the Ordo Templi Orientis is eventually assembled.
suggested_refs: Carl Kellner's correspondence and patents, Vienna, 1890s

stops.name: Berlin, vice-president under Franz Hartmann
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: de.wikipedia gives 30 August 1896 and names the office as vice-president of the German offshoot of the Theosophical Society in America, under Franz Hartmann. The city of the appointment is not given in the source, and the Berlin pin follows his residence of the period.
stops.campa: On the thirtieth of August he is made vice-president of the German offshoot of the Theosophical Society in America, under Franz Hartmann. It is a real office in a real organization, and it is the next twenty-five years in miniature: a German branch of an American body of an Indian doctrine, presided over from Europe, with Reuss second in command and the letterhead already at the printer. Where the appointment is made the source does not say, and the pin follows the city he is living in.
suggested_refs: Records of the German section of the Theosophical Society in America under Franz Hartmann, 1896

stops.name: Paris, the charter from Papus
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: 24 June 1901, per en.wikipedia. No Paris address is recorded for the transaction; the coordinate is the corpus's canonical Paris pin.
stops.campa: Gerard Encausse, who signs himself Papus, names Reuss Special Inspector for the Martinist Order in Germany. The Martinist current is one more line to braid in. Paris in these decades is the switchboard of the European occult revival: Blavatsky is feted here by duchesses in 1884, Rene Guenon will begin sorting real Masonic transmission from political lodges here in 1913, and Reuss now holds a French charter to work German soil with. The document is dated to the day, as all of his documents are.
suggested_refs: Martinist Order charters issued by Gerard Encausse, 1901

stops.name: London, Aldermanbury: the charter from Westcott
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: charter 26 July 1901 and letter of authorization 24 February 1902, per en.wikipedia. The venue is not documented; the pin is the corpus's canonical Societas Rosicruciana in Anglia coordinate, inherited from the Bulwer-Lytton journey.
stops.campa: William Wynn Westcott, coroner for north-east London, co-founder of the Golden Dawn and Supreme Magus of the Societas Rosicruciana in Anglia, gives Reuss a charter for a Swedenborgian Rite working, and a letter of authorization the following February. The pin is Aldermanbury, where the Societas Rosicruciana was founded in 1867 in the milieu this atlas already visits with Bulwer-Lytton, its disputed patron. The place of the transaction is not recorded. What is recorded is a signature.
suggested_refs: Societas Rosicruciana in Anglia records under W. W. Westcott, Supreme Magus

stops.name: Berlin, the Valley of Berlin
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1902 by Koenig's parareligion.ch archive, which gives no day; the default of 1 January stands for an undated year, and the sanctuary may in fact postdate the Yarker patent of that September.
stops.campa: A Sovereign Sanctuary of the Rite of Memphis and Misraim is erected in Berlin under the name the Valley of Berlin. Reuss holds, on paper, a Martinist inspectorate, a Swedenborgian Rite, a Rosicrucian charter and now a sanctuary of his own; the thirty-third degree will arrive in September. He holds, in fact, a few dozen correspondents and a printing bill. The distance between the two is not a fraud he conceals. It is the operating principle, and it is what Peter-R. Koenig will later name a paper empire.
suggested_refs: Oriflamme, the order's journal, issues of 1900, 1902 and 1906

stops.name: Manchester, the letters-patent from John Yarker
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: 24 September 1902, per en.wikipedia; de.wikipedia records the same transfer of the Rite of Memphis and Misraim. The building is not named, and Yarker's Manchester base stands in for it.
stops.campa: John Yarker, who holds the Rite of Memphis and Misraim in England and issues its degrees freely, makes Reuss a Sovereign Grand Inspector General of the thirty-third degree and transfers the rite's German rights to him. This is the charter the Ordo Templi Orientis will point to when asked by what authority it exists. It is also the Egyptian Rite line that Rene Guenon traces back through Alexandria and the 1864 Masonic initiation of Emir Abdelkader, the same current arriving from the far end.
suggested_refs: John Yarker's warrant books for the Rite of Memphis and Misraim, Manchester

stops.name: Hamburg, the Orient of the Phoenix of Truth
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Koenig's parareligion.ch gives 1 July 1904. The founding is not corroborated in either Wikipedia article, no address is named, and the Hamburg city centre stands in for the venue.
stops.campa: On the first of July an Orient styled the Phoenix of Truth is founded at Hamburg, one more chartered body in a lattice that now runs from the Baltic to the Rhine. Koenig's archive records the name and the date; no address, no membership roll and no subsequent working have been produced. The multiplication is itself the point. Each new body is evidence for the authority of the man who chartered it, and that authority is the ground for chartering more.
suggested_refs: Hamburg lodge registers, 1904, for an Orient styled Phoenix of Truth

stops.name: Vienna, the death of Carl Kellner
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1905 by en.wikipedia, which gives no day. Kellner's place of death is not recorded in the sources consulted, and the Vienna pin follows his city.
stops.campa: Kellner dies. The Academia Masonica he financed, the house the two of them have been designing since the Vienna conversations of 1895, passes to Reuss, who becomes sole proprietor of the doctrine and of the debts. Within a year the body will be renamed and constituted as the Ordo Templi Orientis, with Reuss at its head and Kellner promoted, posthumously, into its founding legend. The dead partner is the most useful kind. He can be cited as the source of the sexual secret and he cannot be asked what he actually meant by it.
suggested_refs: Kellner estate papers and the transfer of the Academia Masonica, 1905

stops.name: London, Lingam-Yoni
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1906 by en.wikipedia; no month is given and the place of publication is not specified in the sources consulted. The default of 1 January stands for the undated year.
stops.campa: He publishes Lingam-Yoni, a German rendering of Hargrave Jennings on phallic symbolism, and with it fixes the doctrine the order will be known for: that the central mystery of every religion is sexual, that the Grail is anatomical, and that the ninth degree teaches the technique. Jennings had written for antiquarians. Reuss turns the material into an initiatory system with grades, fees and a warrant to confer them, and sells the book by subscription through the Oriflamme.
stops.quote: Close minded, petty, or malicious, great and small spirits!...the above explanation of the Graal-secret is not to be understood as literal, personal, material, earthly...
stops.quote_source: Theodor Reuss, Parsifal and the Secret of the Graal Unveiled (1914), Main Part, section 'A Warning to all'; the doctrine's later and plainest statement, as reproduced on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: Theodor Reuss, Lingam-Yoni (1906), after Hargrave Jennings

stops.name: Berlin, the warrant to Rudolf Steiner
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1906 by en.wikipedia, which gives no month; February is a placeholder used to order the year's stops and should not be read as a documented date.
stops.campa: Reuss warrants Rudolf Steiner as Deputy Grand Master of a chapter styled Mystica Aeterna, in Berlin. Steiner takes the warrant, removes the sexual material from the ritual entirely, works it for a few years as a Christian and Rosicrucian rite, and lets it lapse. He will spend the rest of his life being asked about it. No charter Reuss issues will travel further, and the man who accepts this one will come to treat it as a formality he should have declined.
suggested_refs: Rudolf Steiner's Mystica Aeterna warrant and the Misraim-Dienst ritual texts

stops.name: London, the constitution and the Outer Head
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia gives the constitution on 21 June 1906 and the self-proclamation as O.H.O. in July 1906, as separate events. De.wikipedia distinguishes an English constitution of 22 January 1906 from a German one of 21 June 1906. Koenig dates the London settlement to the end of 1913 instead, contradicting the January 1906 arrival; the contradiction is not resolved.
stops.campa: On the twenty-first of June he promulgates a constitution for the Ordo Templi Orientis, and in July he proclaims himself its Outer Head: O.H.O., Frater Superior, Merlin Peregrinus. The order now exists in the only sense that matters to him, as a document with a seal, a hierarchy of ten degrees and a man at the top. He has been resident in London since January, by the English account. Koenig's archive dates his London settlement to the end of 1913 instead, and the two accounts are not reconciled.
suggested_refs: The 1906 constitutions of the Ordo Templi Orientis, English and German texts

stops.name: Paris, rue Cadet: the Masonic and Spiritualist conference
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: 24 June 1908, per en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia. The venue is inferred from the Grand Orient de France headquarters in the rue Cadet and is not stated in the sources.
stops.campa: At the international Masonic and Spiritualist conference in Paris he raises Papus to the tenth degree of the Ecclesia Gnostica Catholica, the gnostic church he has attached to the order. The traffic runs both ways now. Papus chartered him in 1901, he consecrates Papus in 1908, and each man's authority is certified by the other. The hall is inferred from the Grand Orient's headquarters in the rue Cadet; the sources give the conference and the date, and no address.
suggested_refs: Proceedings of the 1908 Congres maconnique et spiritualiste international, Paris

stops.name: London, the seventh degree for Aleister Crowley
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1910 by en.wikipedia and by its Ordo Templi Orientis article; no day and no venue are given. The default of 1 January stands for the undated year.
stops.campa: Aleister Crowley is admitted to the first three degrees and then to the seventh of the Ordo Templi Orientis. He is thirty-five, notorious, expensively educated, and a far better writer than anyone else in the order. Reuss has acquired the one collaborator capable of turning a paper empire into a literature. He has also acquired the man who will take it away from him. No ceremonial venue is named in the sources consulted; the initiation is recorded by the order, not by a register.
suggested_refs: Crowley's diaries for 1910; O.T.O. degree records of the same year

stops.name: London, 124 Victoria Street: the ninth degree
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: 1 June 1912, per en.wikipedia. The address is Crowley's documented London flat of the period; the sources do not name it as the site of the meeting.
stops.campa: Reuss comes to Crowley's flat to accuse him of printing the ninth degree secret in The Book of Lies, a book Crowley says he wrote without knowing there was a secret in it to print. The confrontation ends in promotion: the ninth degree, and the office of National Grand Master General for Great Britain and Ireland, with the style Supreme and Holy King of Ireland, Iona and all the Britains within the Sanctuary of the Gnosis. The address is Crowley's own of that year.
suggested_refs: Aleister Crowley, The Book of Lies (1912), and the O.T.O. patent of 1 June 1912

stops.name: London, the Gnostic Mass and the Rite of Memphis and Misraim
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1913: en.wikipedia dates both the Gnostic Mass and the grand mastership of Memphis and Misraim to that year, with no month for either. A 1914 date for the grand mastership circulates and is not supported by the article text.
stops.campa: At Reuss's instance Crowley writes Liber XV, the Gnostic Mass, for the Ecclesia Gnostica Catholica: a priest, a priestess, a lance, a paten, and a communion in which the congregation declares that there is no part of it that is not of the gods. It is the one liturgical text of the order still in continuous use a century afterwards. In the same year Reuss becomes Grand Master of the Rite of Memphis and Misraim, the rite Yarker chartered to him eleven years before.
suggested_refs: Aleister Crowley, Liber XV: Ecclesiae Gnosticae Catholicae Canon Missae (1913)

stops.name: Berlin, the war and the Red Cross
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1914 by en.wikipedia, which has him leave England for Germany and work for the Red Cross in Berlin; the month of the departure is not recorded, and August is taken from the outbreak of the war.
stops.campa: War closes England to him. He leaves for Germany and works for the Red Cross in Berlin, a man of fifty-nine belonging to a country now at war with the country where his order was constituted and where his Grand Master lives. In the same year he publishes Parsifal and the Secret of the Graal Unveiled, the pamphlet that states the sexual reading of Wagner outright and, in the same breath, warns the reader against taking it literally. His English lodges are now enemy territory.
stops.quote: Learn to eat of the tree of Knowledge, and of the tree of Life enjoy the fruit.
stops.quote_source: Theodor Reuss, Parsifal and the Secret of the Graal Unveiled (1914), Closing Word; as reproduced on Wikiquote
suggested_refs: Theodor Reuss, Parsifal und das Enthuellte Graals-Geheimnis (1914)

stops.name: Basel, the neutral ground
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1916 by en.wikipedia, which places him in Germany from 1914 and at Basel only in 1916; no month is given. Accounts dating the Basel move to 1914 conflate it with the wartime transfer of the order's headquarters to neutral territory.
stops.campa: He crosses into Switzerland and settles at Basel, where the order's headquarters is re-established on neutral soil while its English and its German members serve in opposing armies. From Basel he constitutes an Anational Grand Lodge. Anational, because a body claiming a universal mystery cannot be a national one, and because two of his lodges are shooting at each other. Switzerland in these years fills with the war's refusers, and the mountain above Ascona is where they gather.
suggested_refs: Constitution of the Anational Grand Lodge, Basel, 1916

stops.name: Monte Verita, the lodge Verita Mistica
stops.date_confidence: attested for January 1916 by Koenig's parareligion.ch archive, which gives no day; the fifteenth is a placeholder within the month. The coordinate is Wikipedia's Monte Verita position, correcting a pin in the research pool that fell in the valley below.
stops.campa: He climbs to the vegetarian colony above Ascona, where Ida Hoffmann and Henri Oedenkoven have been running a sanatorium of raw food, loose clothing and sunlight since 1900, and founds a lodge there called Verita Mistica. The mountain already holds anarchists, dancers, nudists and Gusto Graeser, whom it has expelled once already. Into this Reuss brings the tenth degree, the Gnostic Mass and a schedule of fees. The lodge fragments within two years, over money.
suggested_refs: Monte Verita colony records, 1916 to 1918; Casa Anatta museum holdings, Ascona

stops.name: Monte Verita, the manifesto Verita Mystica
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: 22 January 1917, per en.wikipedia. The place of issue is not stated and the pin follows the lodge of the same name.
stops.campa: He issues the manifesto Verita Mystica and revises the constitution of the order around it. The announcement he prints for the coming congress states that there are two centres of the Ordo Templi Orientis, both in neutral countries, one in New York and one in Ascona. As a description of what is left it is accurate. The English lodges are silent, the German ones are at the front, and the order has been reduced to a hill in Ticino and a correspondence address in America.
stops.quote: Es gibt zwei Zentren des O.T.O., beide in neutralen Ländern, an die jene, die sich für das Ziel dieses Kongresses interessieren, Anfragen richten können. Das eine befindet sich in New York (U.S. of America), das andere in Ascona (Italienische Schweiz).
stops.quote_source: Announcement text for the 1917 O.T.O. congress at Monte Verita, as quoted in the German Wikipedia article 'Theodor Reuss'; no footnote is attached there to the original printing
suggested_refs: Verita Mystica (1917) and the revised O.T.O. constitution of the same date

stops.name: Monte Verita, the anational congress
stops.date_confidence: attested: en.wikipedia dates the congress to August 1917, and the Monte Verita article gives 15 to 25 August. The programme is reported rather than minuted.
stops.campa: From the fifteenth to the twenty-fifth of August the congress sits on the mountain: nationalism and its cure, the rights of women, mystical freemasonry, dance. Crowley's poetry is read aloud. The Gnostic Mass is performed. Reuss preaches a cult of Mary founded on brotherhood and sisterhood, and Rudolf von Laban's dancers, who are on the hill that summer working out a grammar of movement from crystal and planet, are part of the audience and part of the rite.
stops.quote: Let this new encourage you! We live in your work!
stops.quote_source: Theodor Reuss, undated letter to Aleister Crowley, dated 1917 in the German Wikipedia article 'Theodor Reuss', where no footnote is given
suggested_refs: Programme and press notices of the 1917 anational congress, Ascona

stops.name: Zurich, the Grand Lodge Libertas et Fraternitas
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: 24 October 1917, per en.wikipedia. The coordinate is the corpus's canonical Zurich pin, inherited byte for byte from the Laban journey.
stops.campa: On the twenty-fourth of October he charters a lodge at Zurich under the name Libertas et Fraternitas, moving the working down off the mountain and into a city. Its members include Rudolf von Laban, who is reading the moving body through the same esoteric grammar the order teaches and who takes from this milieu the ritual scaffolding of his dance. Wartime Zurich holds Dada at the Cabaret Voltaire, Lenin in the Spiegelgasse and this lodge, within a few streets of one another.
suggested_refs: Charter of the Grand Lodge Libertas et Fraternitas, Zurich, 24 October 1917

stops.name: Casa Anatta, put off the mountain
stops.date_confidence: disputed: the plain chronology in en.wikipedia has him leave the colony before November 1918 or in 1919 and gives no cause, while the Monte Verita article reports an expulsion by Oedenkoven after midnight rituals. The two accounts are not reconciled here. The coordinate is the corpus's canonical Casa Anatta pin from the Ida Hoffmann journey.
stops.campa: Henri Oedenkoven, who has tolerated a great deal on his mountain, discovers what is being done at midnight in the name of the order and puts Reuss off it, calling him a charlatan and a devourer of women. It is the second banishment Monte Verita has pronounced, after Graeser's. In the same period Reuss publishes his German translation of Crowley's Gnostic Mass, the most durable work of these years. The English chronology says only that he leaves the colony.
stops.quote: a charlatan and devourer of women
stops.quote_source: Henri Oedenkoven on Reuss, as reported in the English Wikipedia article 'Monte Verita'
suggested_refs: Oedenkoven's correspondence on the closure of the O.T.O. working at Monte Verita

stops.name: Lyon, the Antioch succession
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: 18 September 1919, per en.wikipedia. The location of the consecration is not recorded in any source consulted, and the pin is Bricaud's gnostic see at Lyon rather than a documented meeting place.
stops.campa: Jean Bricaud, patriarch of the gnostic church at Lyon, reconsecrates him and conveys the line called the Antioch succession, so that the bishops of the Ecclesia Gnostica Catholica can claim apostolic descent through a Syrian see. Reuss now holds Masonic, Rosicrucian, Martinist, Illuminist and episcopal authority, each certified by a document, and each document signed by a man whose own authority Reuss has certified in return. Where the two met is not recorded.
suggested_refs: Consecration records of Jean Bricaud, Eglise Gnostique Universelle, Lyon, 1919

stops.name: Zurich, the stroke and the last congress
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the congress, 17 July 1920, per en.wikipedia. The stroke is placed in spring 1920 by the same source and flagged there as not entirely certain; Crowley refers to it afterwards as a first stroke of paralysis.
stops.campa: In the spring something happens to him that Crowley later calls his first stroke of paralysis and the English record calls not entirely certain. In July he is in Zurich for the congress of the World Federation of Universal Freemasonry, still arguing for recognition from the regular bodies that have never given it. In the same year he publishes the building programme of the gnostic neo-Christians, whose motto sets Crowley's law of will against a demand for accounting.
stops.quote: Freiheit, Gerechtigkeit, Liebe! Tue, was du willst, doch bedenke, dass du Rechenschaft schuldig bist
stops.quote_source: Theodor Reuss, Aufbauprogramm der gnostischen Neo-Christen (1920), as quoted in the German Wikipedia article 'Theodor Reuss', where no footnote is given
suggested_refs: Acts of the 1920 Zurich congress of the World Federation of Universal Freemasonry

stops.name: Basel, the last charters go out
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: the X charters of 10 May 1921 and the gauge of amity of 30 July 1921, per en.wikipedia. The place of issue is not recorded for either, and the pin follows his Swiss base of the period.
stops.campa: On the tenth of May he issues tenth degree charters to Charles Stansfeld Jones for the United States and to Heinrich Traenker for Germany, and on the thirtieth of July a gauge of amity to H. Spencer Lewis, founder of the Rosicrucian order A.M.O.R.C. in California. He is sixty-five, ill, and still signing. Every one of these documents will be produced after his death as evidence in a succession dispute, which is what such documents are for, though not in the way he intended.
suggested_refs: The 1921 O.T.O. charters to C. S. Jones and Heinrich Traenker; the A.M.O.R.C. gauge of amity

stops.name: Munich, the travel agency
stops.date_confidence: attested for September 1921 by en.wikipedia; no day is given. The coordinate is the corpus's canonical Munich occult-circle pin, inherited from the Maria Orsic journey.
stops.campa: He returns to Germany and settles in Munich, taking work as an employee of the municipal travel agency: the Outer Head of the Order, selling tickets. Munich in 1921 is thick with the material he has spent thirty years chartering. Sebottendorff's Thule Society and its Golden Dawn readers overlap with his own lodge in personnel and in period, and the Vienna and Munich occult ecology this atlas visits with Maria Orsic is the ecology he is retiring into.
suggested_refs: Munich municipal employment records, 1921 to 1923

stops.name: Munich, the letter to Crowley
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: Reuss's letter of 9 November 1921, Crowley's reply of 23 November, and Crowley's diary entry of 27 November, all per en.wikipedia. Reuss's own reply to the reply is not extant.
stops.campa: He writes to Crowley in anger, repudiating the identification of Thelema with the doctrine of the order. Two weeks later Crowley writes back that it is his will to be Outer Head of the Order and that he will avail himself of Reuss's abdication, and four days after that he records in his diary that he has done it. Reuss has not abdicated. He is sixty-six, in Munich, working at a travel bureau, and the order he chartered has been taken by a man he chartered.
stops.quote: I have proclaimed myself O.H.O. Frater Superior of the Order of Oriental Templars.
stops.quote_source: Aleister Crowley, diary entry of 27 November 1921, as quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Theodor Reuss'
suggested_refs: The Reuss-Crowley correspondence of November 1921; Crowley's diaries of the same month

segments.name: Munich, and the Paper Empire After

stops.name: Munich, the resignation that may not exist
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: en.wikipedia reports Crowley's claim of a 1922 resignation and notes the matter is unresolved among the O.T.O. successor bodies; Lawrence Sutin questions it for want of corroboration. No month is given and no document is extant. The Confessions of Aleister Crowley was not directly reachable for this journey.
stops.campa: Crowley states afterwards that Reuss resigned the office in 1922 in his favour. No such resignation is extant. Reuss's reply to the November letter has not survived either, and the successor bodies descending from this year have disagreed ever since over whether the abdication was made, made under duress, or invented. The dispute outlives him unsettled. In 1925 a conference of grand masters elects Crowley Outer Head of the Order over a rival claim.
stops.quote: resigned the office [of O.H.O.] in 1922 in my favour
stops.quote_source: Aleister Crowley, The Confessions of Aleister Crowley, as directly quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Theodor Reuss'; the bracketed gloss is Wikipedia's editorial insertion and the Confessions text itself was not reachable
sources: Lawrence Sutin, as cited in the Ordo Templi Orientis article
suggested_refs: The Confessions of Aleister Crowley, chapters on the O.T.O. succession

stops.name: Munich, death and the grave nobody has found
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and agreed by every source consulted: 28 October 1923, Munich, aged sixty-eight. The burial place is a stated gap in the record rather than a lost or destroyed grave.
stops.campa: He dies in Munich on the twenty-eighth of October, sixty-eight years old, a clerk at a travel agency, holder on paper of more initiatic offices than any man of his century. No source consulted records where he is buried: not the English article, not the German one, not Koenig's archive, which has assembled everything else. There is no plaque, no monument and no grave that anyone has located. The man who issued documents for a living leaves no stone.
suggested_refs: Munich civil death register, October 1923; Munich municipal cemetery records

stops.name: Munich, the verdict and the archive
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the letter, 14 February 1925, quoted on Wikiquote and in en.wikipedia. Koenig's archive has no single date; it has grown online since the 1990s and the stop is anchored to the letter it answers.
stops.campa: Crowley writes to Heinrich Traenker with an assessment of the man whose order he now holds: uncertain in temper, unreliable, latterly out of his depth. It is the epitaph that sticks for sixty years. Then Peter-R. Koenig begins assembling the charters, the letters and the organizational records of 1905 to 1923 into an archive at parareligion.ch, and another figure comes back into view. The archive holds an administrator who understood that an initiation is a document, and who spent forty years issuing them.
stops.quote: Reuss was very uncertain in temper, and in many ways unreliable. In his last years he seems to have completely lost his grip, even accusing The Book of the Law of communistic tendencies, than which no statement could be more absurd.
stops.quote_source: Aleister Crowley, letter to Heinrich Tranker, 14 February 1925; as reproduced on Wikiquote and in the English Wikipedia article 'Theodor Reuss'
suggested_refs: Peter-R. Koenig, The O.T.O. Phenomenon archive, parareligion.ch
